text: Search dishes, ingredients, allergens… Opening Menu · Fall 2026 Pre-Shift Quiz The Bar / Bar basics / Shaken vs. stirred Method matters SHAKEN VS. STIRRED How a drink is mixed changes how it tastes, looks and feels. One simple rule covers most cocktails. THE RULE Shake if it has citrus, juice, egg, dairy or cream. Stir if it’s all spirits. Hard and fast SHAKEN WHEN Citrus, juice, egg, dairy or cream WHAT IT DOES Chills fast, adds air and water. Makes a lively, frothy, slightly cloudy drink. HOW LONG 10–15 seconds, hard, until the tin frosts. TOOLS Shaker tins, Hawthorne strainer, fine strainer. Margarita Daiquiri Whiskey Sour Cosmopolitan Espresso Martini Smooth and slow STIRRED WHEN All spirits, no juice WHAT IT DOES Chills gently with no air. Keeps the drink clear, silky and heavy. HOW LONG 20–30 seconds, until the mixing glass is ice-cold. TOOLS Mixing glass, bar spoon, julep strainer. Old Fashioned Manhattan Martini Negroni Sazerac Beyond the shake OTHER METHODS Built Made right in the glass, over ice. No shaker. Paloma Moscow Mule Aperol Spritz Muddled Fruit, herbs or sugar pressed gently to release flavor. Mojito Dry shake Shaken without ice first, to whip egg white into foam

text: Search dishes, ingredients, allergens… Opening Menu · Fall 2026 Pre-Shift Quiz Wine / Wine service / Open sparkling STEP 03 Sparkling Wine service · 3 of 6 A sigh, not a pop OPEN SPARKLING A sparkling bottle is under high pressure. Open it with a quiet sigh, never a pop, and never point it at anyone. TOOLS A napkin TIME About a minute WHEN Well chilled, at the table CHECK Point it away from people 1 Present 2 Open 3 Sparkling 4 Taste 5 Pour 6 Decant How to do it STEP BY STEP 1 Remove the foil. 2 Put your thumb on the cork and keep it there. 3 Loosen the wire cage, but leave it on the cork. 4 Tilt the bottle 45°, pointed away from guests. 5 Hold the cork and cage still, and slowly turn the bottle. 6 Let the gas out with a quiet hiss. ALWAYS ✓ Keep your thumb on the cork ✓ Point away from guests and lights ✓ Chill it well first NEVER ✕ Pop the cork ✕ Let go once the cage is loose ✕ Shake the bottle SAY IT AT THE TABLE “Cheers! May I pour for the table?” i GOOD TO KNOW A sparkling wine bottle holds several times the pressure of a car tire. A loose cork can cause a serious injury. Never argue. ALWAYS ✓ Pour a small taste ✓ Stay calm and kind ✓ Offer a fresh bottle if it’s faulty NEVER ✕ Argue with the guest ✕ Pour the table before approval ✕ Taste from the guest’s glass What can go wrong KNOW THE FAULTS Corked Wet cardboard, musty basement.
